final_proof:
The phrase “pointwise maximum” in the statement is a terminological slip: the displayed definition uses \(\min\), as do the title and the asserted formula. We therefore use the displayed definition of \(f\wedge g\).

We first establish that, for arbitrary real numbers \(a,b\),
\[
\min\{a,b\}=\frac{a+b-|a-b|}{2}.
\]
Indeed, since the order on \(\mathbb R\) is total, either \(a\le b\) or \(b<a\). If \(a\le b\), then \(a-b\le0\), so \(|a-b|=b-a\), and hence
\[
\frac{a+b-|a-b|}{2}=\frac{a+b-(b-a)}2=a=\min\{a,b\}.
\]
If \(b<a\), then \(a-b>0\), so \(|a-b|=a-b\), and hence
\[
\frac{a+b-|a-b|}{2}=\frac{a+b-(a-b)}2=b=\min\{a,b\}.
\]
Thus the scalar identity holds in all cases.

Now let \(s\in S\) be arbitrary. By the definitions of pointwise addition, subtraction, absolute value, and scalar multiplication,
\[
\left(\frac12\bigl(f+g-|f-g|\bigr)\right)(s)
=\frac12\left(f(s)+g(s)-|f(s)-g(s)|\right).
\]
Applying the scalar identity with \(a=f(s)\) and \(b=g(s)\), this equals \(\min\{f(s),g(s)\}\), which by definition is \((f\wedge g)(s)\). Consequently the two functions agree at every \(s\in S\). By extensionality of functions (also covering the case \(S=\varnothing\)),
\[
f\wedge g=\frac12\bigl(f+g-|f-g|\bigr).
\]
